content.text: {"headline":"Approve P4 (demand smoothing on general): predicted 80.9% service level for 14:30-16:30 at ₹372 extra, the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target.","why":"This is a capacity problem, not a demand one. There were 9 unplanned absences on general against a usual 2.4: 4 called in sick and 5 were sent home unwell. Call volume is on forecast (564 vs 568). With no action, the window is predicted at 79.0%, with general at 74.5%. P4 delays breaks on both queues, adds IVR callback on general, and deflects 15% of balance and new-offer enquiries to chat. That brings general up to 80.4% and keeps payments at 81.3%. Predicted abandon rate falls to 3.5% from 4.2%, and rest-of-day service level rises to 88.6%. Diagnosis confidence is medium because the detector's staffing figures don't match the floor counts after 13:45.","trade_offs":["P1 (₹0) and P2 (₹300) cost less but both miss the target, at 78.1% and 77.4%. Both also move cross-skilled agents off payments, cutting payments to 78.7% and 79.9%.","P3 (overtime) reaches 81.7% with general at 79.6%. It costs ₹1,740, nearly five times P4, and depends on agents accepting overtime offers.","P4 leaves payments staff in place, so the other queue is protected. The customer impact is that some general callers are pushed to callback or chat instead of a live agent.","P4 clears the target by only 0.9 points, so there is little margin if absences grow."],"watch":"Watch general-queue service level and chat uptake from 15:00. If more agents are sent home, or deflection falls short and general drops below about 78%, move to P3's overtime offers."}
